challenge.prompt: Using three.js, build a beautiful 3D model of the Solar System with a cinematic tour. Requirements: the Sun glowing at the centre (emissive, with a halo) lighting the planets; the 8 planets in the correct order (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), with relative sizes that make sense (Jupiter the largest, Mercury the smallest), procedural textures on canvas (Jupiter's bands, Earth's oceans and continents, Mars red), Saturn with its rings, the Moon orbiting the Earth; faint orbit lines; planets orbiting at different speeds; a starfield background; a camera that travels from planet to planet showing each one close up with its name on screen. Use the requestAnimationFrame timestamp for animation time. Full-window canvas that handles resizing. Starts automatically, no interaction needed.

rubric.es: El Sol brilla en el centro (resplandor o halo) e ilumina los planetas
Se ven los planetas en el orden correcto desde el Sol (no faltan ni están cambiados)
Júpiter es el más grande y los planetas rocosos son pequeños
Se reconocen las texturas: bandas de Júpiter, océanos de la Tierra, Marte rojo
Se ve la Luna junto a la Tierra
La cámara viaja de un planeta a otro y los muestra de cerca con su nombre
Hay líneas de órbita y fondo de estrellas
Va fluido (al menos 30 fotogramas por segundo)

prompt:
Using three.js, build a beautiful 3D model of the Solar System with a cinematic tour. Requirements: the Sun glowing at the centre (emissive, with a halo) lighting the planets; the 8 planets in the correct order (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), with relative sizes that make sense (Jupiter the largest, Mercury the smallest), procedural textures on canvas (Jupiter's bands, Earth's oceans and continents, Mars red), Saturn with its rings, the Moon orbiting the Earth; faint orbit lines; planets orbiting at different speeds; a starfield background; a camera that travels from planet to planet showing each one close up with its name on screen. Use the requestAnimationFrame timestamp for animation time. Full-window canvas that handles resizing. Starts automatically, no interaction needed.

three.js (r186) is available as an ES module: use `import * as THREE from 'three'` and addons from 'three/addons/...' (e.g. 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js') inside <script type="module">. An import map is provided for you: do not add your own import map or any CDN URL.

Requirements: deliver everything in ONE self-contained HTML file (inline CSS and JavaScript; no external resources, CDNs, fonts or images). Reply with the complete file in a single ```html code block.

faults: La iluminación en las transiciones de cámara es irregular: en la captura 7 (Venus) y la 10 (Marte), los planetas aparecen casi totalmente oscuros o en sombra mientras la cámara se acerca.
Las texturas de la Tierra (captura 9) y Mercurio (captura 5) se ven algo rudimentarias y 'pintadas' en lugar de detalladas.
En la captura 1, la perspectiva de los planetas en el horizonte está muy aplanada, reduciendo la sensación de profundidad inicial.
Las texturas de los continentes en la Tierra (cap 7) y las manchas de Marte (cap 4) son formas simples y algo toscas.
El plano de las órbitas se ve muy inclinado/achatado en varias tomas (cap 1, 10), dando una perspectiva poco natural.
